description.value: We analyzed the effect of cognitive reserve, measured by years of education, on whole-brain dynamic connectivity in patients with frontotemporal dementia using metastate measures derived from resting-state fMRI.

spans.text: These premises set the stage for the present study, in which we analyzed the effect of CR on whole-brain dynamic connectivity in a large cohort of patients with FTD.

description.value: Patients with probable frontotemporal dementia were consecutively recruited between January 2010 and May 2019; the study was observational and cross-sectional, with resting-state MRI acquired during a single scanning occasion.

In the present study, we considered 128 patients fulfilling current clinical criteria for probable FTD, namely 81 with bvFTD and 47 with PPA ( ).

Education, a proxy measure of CR, is inversely correlated with dynamic fluidity, the higher the years of formal schooling the fewer the number of metastates (i.e., metastate numbers, r = −0.246, p = 0.01 FDR-corrected) and the lower the changes from one metastate to another (i.e., metastate changes, r = −0.288, p = 0.01 FDR-corrected) (see ).

Partial Pearson's correlation analysis was used to assess the relationship between the metastate measures (metastate number, metastate changes, metastate span, and metastate total distance) and education, considering age, gender, mean gray matter volume, disease severity as measured by FTLD-modified CDR, endophenotype (bvFTD or PPA), MRI scanner type, and motion parameter (DVARS) as covariates (IBM SPSS Statistics 22.0, Chicago, USA).

Dynamic connectivity parameters were evaluated in 128 patients with FTD using independent component analysis, sliding-time window correlation, and k-means approach to resting state–magnetic resonance imaging data.
